title: PR 07 2026 Consultation and Engagement Research
description:
Exeter City Council is seeking a suitably experienced supplier to deliver a comprehensive Resident Survey and Budget Consultation Survey for 2026, alongside providing flexible, additional consultation and engagement support as required during the contract period.\r
The core requirements include:\r
\r
Delivery of a representative Resident Survey (approx. 1,100 respondents) in line with LGA benchmarking guidance, using a mix of telephone and face-to-face methods to ensure inclusion of hard-to-reach groups.\r
Delivery of a Budget Consultation Survey to capture residents' preferences for budget priorities, using a mix of telephone and online methods.\r
Benchmarking of resident survey results against other councils and Exeter City Council's 2024 and 2025 surveys to identify trends and changes over time.\r
Provision of additional consultation and engagement support on a flexible, call-off basis. This may include focus groups, workshops, surveys, qualitative research, data analysis, and reporting to support discrete projects across the Council.\r
\r
The Council requires a supplier with proven experience in large-scale representative research, strong analytical and reporting capability, and robust project management to deliver work to agreed timescales and within budget. The contract is designed to provide flexibility to respond to fluctuating consultation demand while maintaining high-quality engagement outputs.

title: CP2334-22 Recycling of District Council's Glass Bottles and Jars
description:
As a Waste Disposal Authority (WDA) DCC is responsible for the disposal of waste that the District Councils of Devon collect, known as Local Authority Collected Waste (LACW). DCC works in partnership with all 8 District Councils in Devon as well as the unitary authorities (UA) of Torbay. The partnership, known as DASWC (The Devon Authorities Strategic Waste Committee), consists of representatives at both officer and councillor level from all Devon District Councils and Torbay Council.\r
\r
From 1st April 2024, Waste Glass from Exeter City Council and the District Councils of East Devon, Mid-Devon, North Devon and Teignbridge will require collection and haulage from their respective Waste Collection Points for Recovery at the Contractor's Waste Recovery Point(s). The Waste Collection Point locations are listed within the specification provided in the contract documents, along with the estimated annual tonnage. Appendix A within the procurement documents provides further detail regarding each Waste Collection Point.\r
\r
The estimated value of this contract as stated within this contract notice is based off only the historic haulage costs payable to the winning contractor. However there are a number of additional elements to the value of the contract that are tied to the published letsrecycle.com rates, due to the variable nature of this value it is not possible to provide expected values for this element of the contract. Any prospective bidder should ensure they have fully read and understood all elements of the specification in order to accurately determine its value.\r
\r
The Contract will be for an initial period of three years with option to extend for a further two years

title: PR612022 - Energy Efficiency Improvement Works Housing Assets
description:
ECC have approved a net zero carbon and retrofit strategy as part of their overall planned capital programme of works. In order to develop this strategy, the client team have agreed to develop future specification of works and to develop a long-term retrofit strategy investment plan, to help understand its future liabilities and deliver its strategic/corporate aims.

The project will be targeted at some of the client's fuel poorest stock and it is proposed to be integrated alongside fabric improvement works.

These works will help ECC to improve the energy efficiency (EPC and SAP ratings) of these properties, and reduce carbon emissions in line with new government targets and corporate objectives and assist their tenants to significantly reduce their fuel bills by:
- Improving the thermal performance to the fabric of all buildings
- Providing affordable warmth and heating for tenants
- Provide on-site generation to assist reduction in energy consumption
- Reduce potential of cold bridging points and condensation/mould
- Improve ventilation and comfort for tenants where applicable
- Assist with the education and behavioural change for tenants
- Maximise green initiative capital & revenue funding where possible

The Principle aim of the contract is to support the strategic net zero and retrofit strategy, with the specific aims of elevating the SAP & EPC ratings of ECC's housing stock to achieve the most financially practicable and reasonable amount of carbon savings possible. In turn the results from the works will be monitored and managed to help inform future asset investment strategy.

The carbon reduction and energy efficiency measures will be targeted across the whole stock and will be elevated to at least a Band C (SAP 69) rating but it is estimated that we will exceed this target with a number of properties achieving a Band B rating. From time to time this specification may be added to, modified or amended. The Contractor should use this specification to develop the works programmes and validate existing SOR or approved framework rates.

This Contract was procured via SWPA LHC Whole House (WH2-WS2) Framework. 2 Year initial Contract with up to 2 period of 12 month extensions.

title: CP2231-22 SW Exeter HIF - A379 Trood Lane Junction and Devon Hotel Roundabout
description:
Construction of essential highway infrastructure on a strategic transport corridor enabling residential development to the South West of Exeter. The works include creation of a new signalised junction, capacity improvements and pedestrian and cyclist facilities on the A379 at Trood Lane and Devon Hotel Roundabout. The works incorporate, embankment widening, reinforced earth slope construction and retaining walls, pavement widening and renewal, new and widened pedestrian and cycle paths, surface water drainage system construction including attenuation and outfall renewal, Civil works and ducting for traffic signals, landscaping and traffic management to facilitate the works.\r
\r
The works in relation to the construction of a new signalised junction at the existing Trood Lane Junction with the A379 include but are not limited to the following:\r
\r
- Widening of the A379 including earthworks widening and construction of reinforced earth slopes.\r
- Resurfacing of the existing A379 throughout the scheme extents.\r
- Construction of a new surface water drainage system to both Trood Lane and the A379 throughout the scheme extents including attenuation and reconstruction of an existing outfall.\r
- Widening and reconstruction of Trood Lane between the A379 and the South West Exeter Development Spine Road, including the creation of new cut slopes and retaining walls.\r
- Construction of traffic Islands, ducting and associated civil works to facilitate the installation of signals to the junction. \r
- Investigation and repair of the existing surface water drainage system plus construction of new surface water drainage gulleys, manholes, pipe runs and outfall.\r
- Bus laybys to both sides of the A379.\r
- A new shared pedestrian / cycle path along Trood Lane and the A379 to provide improved access to the development\r
- Landscaping to verge areas and embankments to reinstate habitat for protected species.\r
\r
The works in relation to the construction of improvements to the Devon Hotel Roundabout to improve the capacity of this junction include but are not limited to the following:\r
\r
- Widening of the northbound A379 approach to the junction to create an additional traffic lane including earthworks widening and construction of a reinforced earth slope.\r
- Pavement resurfacing to the A379, the circulatory carriageway, Dawlish Road and Bad Homburg Way\r
- Modification of the roundabout central island\r
- Construction of traffic Islands, ducting and associated civil works to facilitate the provision of a new signalised pedestrian / cycle crossing of the A379.\r
- Construction of connecting footway / cycleway links to Dawlish Road\r
\r
The Tenderer's tendered total of the Prices must not exceed £2,900,000 for the A379 Trood Lane Junction and £650,000 for Devon Hotel Roundabout. \r
\r
The procurement documents are available at: https://www.supplyingthesouthwest.org.uk. \r
\r
Tenders or requests to participate must be submitted electronically via the abovementioned address.

title: M5 Junction 10 Improvements Scheme
description:
Background

Gloucestershire faces significant challenges to achieve its vision for economic growth. A

Joint Core Strategy (JCS) - a partnership between Gloucester City Council, Cheltenham

Borough Council and Tewkesbury Borough Council was formed to produce a co-ordinated

strategic development plan to show how the region will develop during the period up to

2031. This includes a shared spatial vision targeting 35,175 new homes and 39,500 new jobs

by 2031. Major development of new housing (c.9,000 homes) and employment land

(c.100ha) is proposed in strategic and safeguarded allocations in the West and North West

of Cheltenham, much of which lies within Tewkesbury Borough Council. This, in turn, is

linked to wider economic investment, including a government supported and nationally

significant Cyber Park adjacent to GCHQ, predicted to generate c.7,000 jobs.

The M5 J10 improvement scheme (Scheme or Project) is critical to achieving the vision set

out above. The Scheme was also identified by Highways England in the Birmingham to Exeter

Route Strategy as being critical to: (a) maintaining the safe and efficient operation of the M5

corridor; and (b) enabling the planned development and economic growth around Cheltenham, Gloucester and Tewkesbury.

A Business Case for the Scheme was submitted in March 2019 to the Housing Infrastructure

Fund, wherein the investment case was made. Funding was awarded successfully by HIF in

March 2020.

Further general information regarding background to the Scheme and its current status in

the project lifecycle can be found at the following web link:-

www.gloucestershire.gov.uk/J10

Scheme Objectives

• Support economic growth and facilitate growth in jobs and housing by providing improved

transport network connections in west and north-west Cheltenham.

• Provide the transport connections and network capacity in west and north-west

Cheltenham to facilitate the delivery of housing and economic development sites allocated

or safeguarded in the Joint Core Strategy.

• Provide a transport network in the west and north-west Cheltenham area with the levels of

service, safety and accessibility to meet current and future needs.

• Deliver a package of measures which is in keeping with the local environment , minimises

any adverse environmental impacts and meets GCC's ambition on sustainable growth,

decarbonisation and net bio-diversity net gain.

• Provide greater connectivity between Highways England's Strategic Road Network (M5)

and the transport network in west and north-west Cheltenham.

• Provide a more integrated transport network by providing opportunities to switch to more

sustainable transport modes within and to west, north-west and central Cheltenham.

The Authority is conducting the procurement using the restricted procedure in accordance with the requirements of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015 (SI 2015/102) (PCR 2015) for the purpose of procuring the services and works described

The Cornwall FLOW Accelerator project is a collaborative   project   including Celtic Sea Power Limited, University of Exeter, University of Plymouth and the Offshore Renewable Catapult.  It aims to develop tools, knowledge and data which accelerate the Celtic Sea Floating Offshore Wind (FLOW) opportunity and lay significant groundwork with respect to developing a pipeline at both a FLOW project and supply chain level.  The project is part funded by the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF).

title: 98a Clinton Estates
description:
Clinton Devon Estates will undertake a Landscape Recovery scale test utilising 2 catchment scale plans, 20 farm scale plans and a natural capital valuation report generated in their previous test. They will work alongside the certified B company 3keel, Eftec and Exeter University to identify market opportunities and demand for Nature Based Solutions based on these existing outputs. These findings will be disseminated to 20 tenants from the estate to ascertain, in conjunction with advisers from Devon Wildlife Trust and Westcountry Rivers Trust, which options they think are most appropriate for their lands. These outputs will then be used to attempt to transact with private investors in nature based solutions. Clinton Devon Estates will provide a real-life case study of the opportunities and constraints of transacting on ecosystem service benefits related to Environmental Land Management and translating these into commercial opportunities for the tenant farmers of Clinton Devon Estates.

Output: Survey report, outputs from 3 x farmer workshops, market opportunity analysis report, natural capital demand report and a final report detailing all of the findings.

Geographic Coverage: Clinton Devon Estates is located in South West England close to the town of Budleigh Salterton

Policy Priorities: The proposal will contribute to scheme development in the following areas:

Pyts / IDM 	How can a blended finance approach be applied to both individual and collaborative group LNR agreements?
		What industry standards and farm level metrics used by private schemes should LNR consider to support alignment with private market best practice
		How can farmers and land managers stack public and private finance alongside the delivery of SFI and LNR?
		How to blend public and private finance in funding projects
		What barriers, from local to landscape scale, are present with the blended finance approach?
		What mechanisms are most effective for facilitating a blended finance approach across all three schemes? 
		How can a blended finance approach be used to drive delivery of multiple environmental outcomes?
		Testing how we value payments on a natural capital basis - how could a natural capital benefit top up be calculated and implemented in practice
